logon.automatic.name: Automatic sign-in
logon.automatic.titlePass: Windows asks who you are at start-up
logon.automatic.titleFail: Windows signs in automatically at start-up
logon.automatic.why: With automatic sign-in, anyone who turns the PC on is signed in as you. The password is also kept on the PC in readable form.
fix: Press Windows+R, type netplwiz and press Enter.
Tick "Users must enter a user name and password to use this computer" and select OK.
Change your password, since the old one was stored on the PC.

firewall.enabled.name: Firewall
firewall.enabled.why: A firewall stops other devices on the same network from reaching your PC. It matters most on public Wi-Fi.
fix: Open Windows Security and select Firewall & network protection.
Select each network shown as off and turn Microsoft Defender Firewall on.

antivirus.active.name: Antivirus
antivirus.active.titleFail: Antivirus is off or out of date
antivirus.active.why: Antivirus blocks known malware before it runs. Out-of-date definitions miss recent threats.
fix: Open Windows Security and select Virus & threat protection.
Turn real-time protection on, or follow the action shown for your antivirus.
Select Protection updates and check for updates.

disk.encryption.name: Disk encryption
disk.encryption.why: Without encryption, anyone who takes the PC or its drive can read every file on it.
fix: Open Settings > Privacy & security > Device encryption and turn it on.
If that page is missing, search for Manage BitLocker and turn BitLocker on for each drive.
Store the recovery key where your organisation asks you to.
disk.encryption.timeToFix: 10 min, then encrypts in the background

ssh.keys.passphrase.name: SSH key passphrases
ssh.keys.passphrase.titleFail: An SSH key has no passphrase
ssh.keys.passphrase.why: An SSH key without a passphrase works for anyone who copies the file. Malware looks for these files first.
fix: Open a terminal.
Run ssh-keygen -p -f followed by the path of the key file, and enter a new passphrase.
Or move the key into a password manager or SSH agent and delete the file.

ssh.keys.strength.name: SSH key strength
ssh.keys.strength.why: Short RSA keys and DSA keys can be broken with enough computing power, and current servers refuse some of them.
fix: Open a terminal and run ssh-keygen -t ed25519 to create a new key.
Add the new public key wherever the old one was used.
Remove the old key from those places, then delete its files.

ssh.config.name: SSH client settings
ssh.config.why: Forwarding your agent lets every server you connect to use your keys. Without host key checking, an impostor server goes unnoticed.
fix: Open the file named under "Found" in a text editor.
Remove ForwardAgent from settings that apply to every host; use ProxyJump or set it for one host.
Remove "StrictHostKeyChecking no" and "UserKnownHostsFile /dev/null" from settings that apply to every host.
